cards.explanation: The answer is Miriam. The text says it plainly: "There Miriam died and was buried." She's Moses and Aaron's sister (Numbers 26:59), and the text gives her passing just one short sentence. I think that's a heavy way to begin this stretch of the story.

The answer is water, friends. "Now there was no water for the congregation…" Everything else in this scene grows out of that one problem. People can put up with a lot, but a whole crowd with empty cups gets loud FAST. Verse 2 says they gathered against Moses and Aaron.

The answer is False. The text says "…they gathered against Moses and Aaron." Against, not alongside. Verse 3 adds that the people quarreled with Moses. It's a crowd with a complaint, not a prayer meeting.

The answer is their livestock. The people ask why they were brought into the wilderness "…for us and our livestock to die here?" Their animals are on their minds too. I think when the animals are thirsty, the worry gets louder.

The answer is Egypt. The people ask, "Why have you led us up out of Egypt to bring us to this wretched place?" They're pointing back at where they came from and then at where they are now. A thirsty crowd will compare anything to anything.

The answer is the glory of the LORD. Moses and Aaron fall facedown, and "…the glory of the LORD appeared to them." They walked away from the quarreling crowd and got an answer at the Tent of Meeting. That is a good place to take a problem, friends.

The answer is to speak to the rock. The LORD says, "You and your brother Aaron are to speak to the rock while they watch, and it will pour out its water." Keep that instruction in your pocket, because it matters in a few verses. It's a short command, so it's easy to remember.

The answer is "you rebels." Moses says, "Listen now, you rebels, must we bring you water out of this rock?" Those are sharp words to say to a whole assembly. Notice the question that follows them, too.

The answer is strikes. "…Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff…" And here's the catch, friends. The LORD had told Moses and Aaron to speak to the rock (Numbers 20:8). Speak, not strike. The water still gushed out, but Moses did something different from what he was told, and the scene isn't done yet.

The answer is True. "…a great amount of water gushed out, and the congregation and their livestock were able to drink." A great amount, friends. The thirsty crowd and their animals could finally drink, and I bet that was a LOUD sigh of relief. The scene doesn't end here, though.

The answer is that they did not trust Him to show His holiness to Israel. The LORD says, "Because you did not trust Me to show My holiness in the sight of the Israelites…" That is the reason the LORD gives. It's a serious verse, so let's take it slowly.

The answer is False. The LORD says to Moses and Aaron, "…you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them." The land is still given to the people, but these two won't be the ones bringing them in. Verse 13 then calls these the waters of Meribah.
